extract:
The Hives are a garage rock band from Fagersta, a small industrial town in central Sweden. They formed in 1993 and have stayed active ever since. The classic lineup was singer Howlin' Pelle Almqvist, his brother Nicholaus Arson on lead guitar, Vigilante Carlstroem on rhythm guitar, Dr. Matt Destruction on bass and Chris Dangerous on drums. Dr. Matt Destruction left in 2013 and was replaced by The Johan and Only. From the start the band built a mythology around themselves. They wore matching black-and-white outfits, and they claimed that a shadowy svengali named Randy Fitzsimmons had assembled them and wrote their songs, a figure credited on their records as songwriter.

The band's roots lie in 1960s garage rock in the vein of The Sonics, the proto-punk of The Stooges, and the fast, melodic punk that thrived in Sweden in the 1990s. That scene centred on Burning Heart Records, the Örebro label that also housed Refused, and it signed The Hives early. The demo-era EP Oh Lord! When? How? was followed by the debut album Barely Legal in 1997, a breakneck, hardcore-inflected record. The 1998 EP A.K.A. I-D-I-O-T sharpened their attack. By Veni Vidi Vicious in 2000 they had distilled their sound into tight, two-minute bursts of riffing and Almqvist's yelping showmanship, anchored by Hate To Say I Told You So and Main Offender.

Their international breakthrough came in 2001. Alan McGee's UK label Poptones issued the compilation Your New Favourite Band, which gathered tracks from their Burning Heart releases. It arrived just as the press was celebrating a garage rock revival alongside The Strokes, The White Stripes and The Vines. Hate To Say I Told You So became a hit in Britain and on American alternative radio, and the band signed a major-label deal through Interscope and Polydor. Tyrannosaurus Hives followed in 2004. It was a more clipped, new wave-tinged album featuring Walk Idiot Walk and Two-Timing Touch And Broken Bones.

The Black and White Album in 2007 broadened their palette further. Several tracks were produced by Pharrell Williams, and the album also included Tick Tick Boom. That song became their most licensed track, turning up widely in sports broadcasts, video games and advertising. In 2008 they recorded the holiday single A Christmas Duel with Cyndi Lauper. A covers EP, Tarred And Feathered, followed in 2010. The band then left the major-label system and released Lex Hives in 2012 on their own imprint, Disques Hives. The single Blood Red Moon appeared in 2015.

Critics have consistently praised The Hives' economy and energy. Their greatest renown, however, comes from their live show. Almqvist's preening, crowd-baiting frontman persona and the band's relentless tempo have made them a perennial festival draw and one of the most reliable live acts of their generation. Alongside The Strokes and The White Stripes, they helped define the early-2000s garage revival and showed that Sweden could export guitar rock as well as pop.

After a long recording gap, the band returned in 2023 with The Death of Randy Fitzsimmons. The album extended their founding myth by framing itself around the disappearance of their fictional mentor. It was well received as a return to the snarling form of their early records. The Hives continue to tour internationally, still in matching suits and still performing at the frantic pace that first made their name.
title: The Hives
